text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two of the suspects accused of fraud in connection with the renovation of the Katutura Single Quarters have been released on bail of N$100.00 each.

- The Director of Elections, Gerhard Toetemeyer, has denied claims by the opposition DTA that his Directorate had been instructed by the government to conduct local authority elections planned for December on a party list system.

- President Sam Nujoma's remarks directed against homosexuals at a recent Party Women's Congress have been endorsed by SWAPO. A statement signed by the party's secretary for information and publicity says gay supporters were destroying the local culture and appropriating foreign ideas in the Namibian society.
- Three more houses from the turn of the century are disappearing from Central Windhoek, to make room for modern developments.
